Your home shouldn’t feel so difficult to manage.

Every day you’re making the same decisions — what to clean, when to do it, who’s doing what. It’s not that your home is too messy. It’s that too much of it lives in your head.

Making Home Easier is 9 days with me. Six short lessons. Three live work sessions. And by the end you’ll have your own Home Rhythm — the decisions that keep your home running, made once, written down, and done. We start September 1st.

🔗Comment EASIER and I’ll send you the link

Your home might not need more of your time. It might need fewer of your decisions.

Think about how many things you decide over and over again:
What’s for dinner? 
When should I do laundry? 
When am I cleaning this? 
Where does this go? 
Who’s responsible for that? 
What am I forgetting?
Did they take the trash out?

Those little open decisions add up and they can make home feel much harder to manage than it needs to.

That’s why I created Making Home Easier, a brand-new 9-day live experience starting September 1.

We’re going to sit down together and figure out what’s taking up space in your head, make some decisions, create simple rhythms and defaults, and give your home less to ask of you.

This isn’t about giving you more to do. It’s about giving you less to manage.
.

What if the reason your home feels like so much isn't just everything you have to do, it's everything you have to keep thinking about?⁠
⁠
What's for dinner? When am I doing laundry? Where does this go? When am I cleaning that? Who's responsible for this? What am I forgetting?⁠
⁠
We make so many of the same household decisions over and over again and every decision we leave open becomes something we have to keep managing.⁠
⁠
I've been thinking about this a LOT lately because it's one of the reasons the Clean Mama Routine has worked in my own home for more than 20 years.⁠
⁠
I don't decide when to clean bathrooms. Monday.⁠
I don't decide when to wash sheets and towels. Saturday.⁠
Those decisions have already been made.⁠

So I started asking myself:⁠
What else in our homes could work this way?⁠

That's what we're going to figure out together in Making Home Easier, my brand-new 9-day live experience starting September 1.⁠

Less to remember. Less to decide. Less to manage.⁠

Tell me I’m not the only one….
Other family members know how to load, unload and run the dishwasher. So why does it still feel like it’s mine?

Doing a task and owning a task aren’t the same thing. Owning it means noticing it needs to happen, doing it, and finishing it — all three, without a check-in from me.

If I’m still the one noticing it’s full, reminding them to run it, and checking that they did? I’m still the owner. The dishwasher just has an assistant.

✔️What’s something in your house you’re technically not doing, but you’re still the one running?

Hi 👋 My name is Becky - you can call me Clean Mama.
I’ve been thinking a lot about why keeping a home can feel so exhausting — and I don’t think the answer is always that we have too much to do.

I think we’re making too many of the same decisions over and over again.
One of the reasons the Clean Mama Routine works is that those decisions are already made.

Monday? Bathrooms.
Saturday? Sheets and towels.
I haven’t decided when to wash my sheets in over 20 years. I decided once.

And lately I’ve been wondering:
What else in our homes could we decide once?
Meals. Laundry. Papers. Schedules. Stuff. Family responsibilities.
Your home gets harder to manage every time you leave something undecided.
I’m going to be talking about this a lot over the next couple weeks because I think there’s something here for us to discover together.

✨Tell me in the comments: what are you tired of having to remember at home?

I do this the same way every time.

It might seem small, but it’s one less decision. Same fold, same hanger placement, every time — no wrinkled pile, no “I’ll deal with it later.”
